facts.statement: The genus Aktaua is known from only one species, Aktaua kizylkumensis.
facts.quote: It is currently known from a single species, A. kizylkumensis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Aktaua have been found in the White Mountain Formation in Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: It is found in the White Mountain Formation of Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: The species name kizylkumensis refers to the Kizylkum Desert where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The species was named for the Kizylkum Desert, in which it was found.

facts.statement: The genus name Aktaua comes from the Uzbek word for 'white,' describing the color of the White Mountain Formation.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the Uzbek word for "white," in reference to the formation it was found in.

facts.statement: Aktaua is an extinct genus of sawfish that lived during the Lutetian stage of the Eocene epoch.
facts.quote: Aktaua is an extinct genus of sawfish from the Lutetian stage of the Eocene epoch.

facts.statement: Aktaua belongs to the family Myliobatidae.
Aktaua is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Aktaua lived between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago during the Lutetian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of Aktaua in the Paleobiology Database.
The genus Aktaua was described by Case and colleagues in 1996.
